content:
What to Expect During the SAGE Labs to Starbased Transition (Version 1.2)  On April 2, Starbased (based.staratlas.com) begins giving players access to Missions every epoch.
a. On Starbased launch, Faction Fleet will receive a 50% reduction in ATLAS emissions (66.67% reduction from inception)., On April 16, the Starbased SDU mechanic commences, and RFR ends in SAGE Labs, Transition Period (Two Weeks: April 2 to April 16)
a. Between April 2 and 16, ALL economic functions will be active in SAGE Labs & Starbased: mining, crafting, SDU scanning, and similar actions.
b. Players can perform ALL actions in both Starbased and Labs with the same variables/rates and under equal SDU Scanning limitations.  
c. On April 16, Starbased will update these variables/rates and will update SDU parameters, while Labs will zero out variables/rates., On April 16, SAGE Labs updates all mining and scanning values to zero (so players can still take those actions, but there will be zero extraction/reward). Movement and transportation will persist until all players withdraw their assets from Labs or until the SA Team can identify a path to force assets back into user wallets., @[AEP] Moustacheride

author: [AEP] Mendizo
content:
I know there was discussion prior about LP being granted differently by sector, such as further out sectors granting more LP. What about using distance from nearest source of resource as well? For example, in an outlying sector far from the CSS, contributing food should grant more LP than at the CSS, but if that sector also has biomass, it should reward less LP than a different outlying sector that doesn't have biomass. 

If we're thinking about the concept of LP as a 'reward' that the faction leaders are giving out to captains and fleets for contributing, and if that LP were to differ for outlying sectors because they're more 'difficult', then it would stand to reason LP should also scale based on closeness to resource availability. This will also help reward those who are contributing things like food that don't grant as much LP; right now it's hard for me to contribute food because it takes up valuable cargo space and gives crap LP rewards, but if that was boosted the farther out I ship it (from CSS and any available food sources), that would help encourage me to do so.

author: Kr1gs
content: The psychology behind what is defined as "work" and "play" is absolutely fascinating to me. I have always wondered what makes people want to play games that resemble real life to the point where they are excited about doing it, and yet struggle to increase their networth IRL. And I have concluded that the difference is whether or not you are doing something because you want to do it, or doing something because you have to do it. So this can apply in a game too. people can "play" a game, and in fact not enjoy it, because they are doing things they "have" to do, and not things they "want" to do. this is especially true in the current meta of MMORPGs today, where everything turns into something that "needs" to be done, in order to progress.

author: 𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐄 | Virtuwul [ROME]
content: I do think this is an interesting point. I have never felt comfortable with this faction ideology concept as been so potent as to create faction on faction warfare as the driving force of combat ideology. I do think there should be some 'symbiotic' benefits to being in the same faction, maybe XP boosts or partnership benefits, but generally it would make for very interesting dynamic gameplay if elements of Oni and Ustur could work together against other elements of Oni and Ustur.

author: [AEP] Boen
content: Guilds are like countries.  Factions are like continents.  Warfare will be like world wars.  Various guilds of various continents banding together and fighting other similar groups. (Russia, China, Venezuela, etc... VS. USA, Europe, etc.)  And some guilds will be more like the UN.  We should still keep a lot of the faction design: Races,Unique resources that can create certain types of ships and assets, But I think the economic split should deprecated and create a real free economy.

author: 𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐄 | Virtuwul [ROME]
content: Yes. You can take away the need for the economic split if you take away the structure that warfare can only exist between faction on faction. Player population imbalances perhaps wouldn't matter as much then if Ustur is smaller than Oni for example as combat would rely on guild alliances vs faction representation. Players would still benefit from the characteristics and intrinsic value each faction type provides. And each faction could still have its characteristics dominate their own LRZ, regardless of the combat superiority that may evolve for a particular faction.

One thing I will add that I’ve noticed in gen chat. The people not in the hardcore SA circle are finding this new way difficult to earn. Before in labs you can sell r4 or other things. People like us can find our way but the people popping up in gen chat that I’ve noticed are struggling

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: Teamwork won't solve the issue.  The rate of burn is still WAY too high (especially at CSS) and the cost to mine Biomass, transport it and craft it is insane compared to the benefit.  Also there is no way to fully coordinate within a Faction.  There are so many people that can only play for an hour here or there and don't have the means to coordinate.  Sure there should be a benefit to coordination, but it should not be 100% mandatory to access even the most basic functions of the game such as crafting.  Simple fix:  Boost LP for Food, reduce the burn rate and instead of not being able to craft when food supply run out, change it to a 50% time penalty when food runs out. By patching that hole you will get a much better data set of how the game then plays and you can move to the next balancing items.

author: 𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐄 | Virtuwul [ROME]
content: Game is a haven for small asset holders they have the way better roi. And have a bunch of advantages based on the scaling the team used. It’s a slippery slope that the team needs to tread by either make the game small asset owner friendly to small asset owner empowered. People forget any advantage that people who can’t purchase a 100k ship or even a 10k or 30k ship thet “whales” can take advantage of the same advantages the smaller player will use just on a larger scale. At the same time you don’t want tonpiss off the person that bought 100k+ ships from you and has taken multitudes of risk above and beyond the $15 or $5 gamer. Would be great to pause the whale argument for a while especially with regards to LP. If the team moves away from the faction gated allocations of LP which actually subsidize smaller players and make it harder for whales and move to a 1 lp pool smaller players will get drowned.

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: Here's a RED HOT TAKE:   There will be an evolution of the Star Atlas economic model.  Most SMALL players will quit SAGE.  NOT THIS YEAR... but when the bear market comes in 2025.  It just won't be worth their time and they won't make enough to keep the grind going.  Some will... but many won't.  Only mid to large players will continue in SAGE until the next bull cycle.  Is that bad?  NOT IF... we get a solid base of UE5 players that spend $5-$20 a month on R4 and other assets.  If we get tens of thousands of people playing the racing game and buying R4.,If we get tens of thousands of players playing SURGE and buying R4., Most players will be happy to play those game modes and maybe earn or lose a few bucks a month.  Plus they will "build long term equity" in their characters/crew.  HERE IS ONE WAY THE SMALL GUYS COULD MAKE MONEY AND HAVE A BLAST: Big Game Hunting/Monster Hunting game mode.  Big Game Hunting will be the more classic "MMO mode" in Star Atlas for the foreseeable future.  How could that be profitable?  UNIQUE RESOURCES that can ONLY be gathered in that game mode: unique resources, DATA, blueprints, pills, potions, etc...  that they can sell to the bigger players for in game advantages., That will create a full circular economy between the smaller players and the bigger players.  Many of the bigger players (myself included) won't have time to grind UE5 game modes.    In short, I believe the economy will evolve into: PRODUCERS (SAGE players) and CONSUMERS (UE5 gamers).  Thoughts?      @PG I BULK @SW4GN3R @[AEP] Mandalorian (Djin Djarin)

author: [AEP] Mendizo
content:
@Matt | IntergalacticHerald, to your question on composability, this is something many technologies (especially in the real world) are moving towards, as the opposite of a single, monolithic program. (I deal with this in SaaS software IRL so it's very much a top of mind topic for me). The main benefits relevant to SA are:

1) Deploying a single, monolithic program makes it much harder to be agile and iterate quickly. As we've seen with things like Labs and Starbased, these could be considered 'composable' modules the team has built. If they were a single monolith, there'd be a lot longer lead times, more expensive dev, etc.
2) As Michael said, this concept of composability also extends to the ecosystem, where targeted/specific 'apps' (we'll use the term loosely) can be developed by the team or the community, resulting in things like Eveeye, the SLY automation tool, etc. If all code were bound in a single monolithic program that only SA could touch, then we could only move as fast as the SA team. Instead, with this composable structure on-chain, the community can fill these gaps.
3) Ultimately, a composable approach lessens absolute interdependencies from the various components. This is critical for something like SA, where the project will have multiple phases, separate UX's and varying capabilities, yet everything still needs to tie to a common backbone.

Hope that helps with a little color as well!

author: [AEP] Freeman [FRNT]
content: It's basically wallet agnostic auto-sign where you can set which instructions are allowed to be auto-sign. The app will dynamically determine which wallet to use (hot wallet we generate or your real wallet) for each transaction. For example if you think crafting should require your ledger to sign but movement shouldn't you can set the hot wallet to do movement and not crafting. Then while you're playing the game movement requires no sign dialog but when you click to craft it will require your ledger.

author: [AEP] Mandalorian (Djin Djarin)
content: We had crafting recipes shuffle around months back. Originally you were supposed to unlock Starbase upgrade recipes after you sourced them from other SB for each upgrade tier. This was changed, but we kept R4 tiers the same, but now creates this disconnect in the technological progression. The idea with R4 is that it creates more interesting economic bootstrapping scenarios when you don't immediately have access to all R4s at a SB. We've decided to reexamine this assumption more meticulously for the combat/territory releases where it will really matter.

author: [AEP] Mendizo
content:
This discussion is probably being dissected by the team for what best excuse... I mean reason... to announce next week. I had ChatGPT summarize the main points for the team to make it easier.

---

The main concerns outlined in the Discord conversation revolve around the recent announcement regarding the acquisition of Multichain Ventures by Star Atlas (SA), particularly in relation to its potential impact on the SA community. Here are the key points:

Value Addition vs. Economic Burden: Members question whether the acquisition of Multichain Ventures brings commensurate value to SA relative to its potential economic burden on the community. They doubt if the assets acquired justify the claimed value.

Transparency and Communication: There's dissatisfaction with the timing and transparency of the announcement. Many feel it was strategically timed and lacked clear communication about the benefits to the community.

Benefit Allocation: Concerns are raised about the perceived benefits accruing primarily to Tokes holders and old stakeholders of Multichain Ventures, rather than the broader SA community. There's a sense of unfairness in the distribution of benefits.

author: [AEP] Mendizo
content:
Impact on Community and Economy: Members express worries about dilution of community assets and the potential negative impact on the SA economy due to the acquisition. Some perceive it as a bailout for Multichain Ventures or an indirect subsidy for Tokes holders.

Community Involvement: There's a desire for more community involvement or benefit-sharing in decisions that affect the SA ecosystem. Suggestions include airdrops to community members or other gestures to involve them in the process.

Runway Concerns: Some members express concern about the dilution of community assets without clear benefits or runway extension for SA. They question the significance of runway in the current scenario.

Overall, there's skepticism about the acquisition's alignment with the interests of the SA community, with members questioning its transparency, fairness, and potential impact on the economy. There's a call for clearer communication, fairer distribution of benefits, and greater community involvement in decisions affecting the ecosystem.

Positives - not many... don't see it bringing in many users initially. I actually don't think it really does anything for Star Atlas.

Put the dev resources into our current assets or the game. Not another community.

author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content: On a personal and reputational level, I do think it’s important to demonstrate that myself and our other founders are not in the business of launching tokens and abandoning them. This has been a criticism/accusation I’ve seen a number of times. That’s not who I am. I think this move, combined with our fortitude through the bear market, truly showcases what we’re all about.

author: [HEIM] SDU pimpUstur
content: We are trying to minimize the total quantities of these cultivation facilities getting released. While I know the total circulating supply of tokes, I don’t know how many people will participate in the transition. Meaning we could end up with a lot of extra assets if we mint for the full quantity of tokes outstanding and only see 10-20% activation of those wallets. It’s hard to estimate, because I’m sure we have had substantial fall off from people following tokes development.  On the other hand, if we try to restrict our mint quantities, and open access to SA users today, we might end up with a deficit of assets for which tokes holders can redeem. We’d then need a new solution for that.  6 months might be too long. I can be flexible on that part. And we can maybe open access or crafting capabilities for these facilities sooner. Or we could mint more and burn anything remaining after 6 months. But trust me, the goal is not to force people in to tokes. We make zero from that, as every tokes redeemed just gets burned by us. They won’t be recirculated

author: [AEP] Boen
content:
Team, what if you made the food consumption rate at an SB a reflection of the number of crew at the SB. So have a minimum consumption rate, call it 50 f/s, and for each crew member 'undocked' at that SB, there is X/s food consumption rate. This would then more reasonably reflect if the SB is been used for crafting / upgraded by a small or large crew contingent and have a better reflection of food input requirements by players. Then players are also really only paying for their crew consumption rate plus the minimum rate/second level (let's assume there is an NFT crew at the SB that maintains the base for example) @Chri.z
You are still getting the food burn mechanism that you want to see, but it is more appropriately spread to the SBs that are been utilized. Because an issue with the current mechanic of equal burn rates across all SBs is that you have to make it high enough to get the burn you want (relative to the input power of the whales), but that then means the little fish have to almost follow the whales around to the SBs where they are contributing food because the food burn is too high to upkeep for the smaller players when whales are not utilizing a SB. Consumption based on player / crew presence will allow for more equal distribution and allow for more active engagement across multiple SBs (and for example, there are a lot of dead SBs right now - whales are understandably only focused on a few specific ones but typically at distances from the CSS that small players don't have the shipping capacity to project over that distance). Also it is just a reasonable mechanic - more crew, more mouths to feed
Same argument can be made for SB upgrade. Tool consumption should be related to crew count

author: [HEIM] SDU pimpUstur
content: Buddy, just to clarify, the difference between selling assets via GAO type procedure and airdroping these assets for free is huge. Selling GAO assets is like a company issuing and selling new stock: on one hand it dilutes their percentage stock holdings but on the other hand it makes this percentage worth more because the sale proceeds are retained by the company and (with some qualifiers) make the stock holder better off in the long run. Airdroping assets on the other hand is like a company issuing stock and gifting it. In the latter case there are no benefits for the stock holder. Now, we have a game here, not a stock, but it is a crowdfunded game and specific promises have been made regarding how atlas emissions will be alocated, and allowing non-investors to participate in earning LP is in my view a clear deviation from these promises.

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content: It's a sort of finite state machine where not only the action matters but also your state when you undertake that action. If you are in an Idle state, docking and undocking do not cost fuel; however, if you are in a 'post warp' state, then fuel is also deducted during docking.

author: ROME | Aegir
content: The Starbased program creates a burn transaction when you dock; I think that's how it simulates fuel consumption. If you don't have fuel, you're missing a precondition for docking (or any other action that requires fuel), and I think you end up stuck, needing to self-destruct your fleet. This is because fuel isn't subtracted continuously during the process, but rather in a discrete state at the end of the actions you've performed. I believe you can chain multiple subwarp actions, but your fuel only gets deducted after the last one. If you don't have enough fuel for it, your only option is to self-destruct the fleet. That's how I understand the game should work, but we need a developer to confirm my hypothesis.

author: 𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐄 | Virtuwul [ROME]
content: yes, and no, I agree there need to be niche economies that aren't worth it for whales, where the roi return is greater than a whale can generate from 'general broad economic/miltary gameplay'. But I don't think that is a matter of time intensive as more it is a matter of niche opportunities with the opportunity cost for a whale to try to dominate it been greater than simply running a broad based conglomerate.  Look, this is a constant debate in irl economics anyway, primarily in the form of what the 'estate / wealth tax' should be. The ability to produce wealth compounds with having wealth, until new areas of opporutnity open up that legacy traditionalists don't take advantage of and then wealth is quickly redistributed (think apple iphone new tech wealth displacing landline AT&E bell companies). So if we don't have that form of creative destruction in the SA economy, which we won't for a while because it is too young, than you are left with an economy that will tend towards oligopoly and vast centralization of wealth (and wealth opportunity) in the few if you are not careful.

author: The Man | RomeONI
content:
I believe that you will likely have whales with botted accounts specializing in each niche. If that is the most profitable way to go that's what will happen. I agree that specialization is good, just don't assume that more simple side loops will be a change to whales abilities to get the best returns. The bigger question is, who cares if whales are able to be the most optimized? I don't. Just make a game that minnows and dolphins can do well in as the goal, and where being a whale doesn't put you to egregiously far ahead in the size scaling and I think we are in a good place. 

Make a game where bots do not make the difference between good roi or not, as it is now. Who benefits from a system that is almost requiring bot usage to be effective? Probably whales more than anyone. Most new players are not going to be setting up automation for their small fleet, they will be looking to have fun and make decisions as they play. A repetitive chain of actions for optimization is not a fun game, that's a task. Bots excel at tasks.

This approach was critical in cultivating a loyal following and enhancing the gaming experience to meet player expectations.    Star Atlas is pursuing this proven strategy.  And if the day comes when SA's success doesn't allow us direct interaction with its leadership (as MW mentioned once), like Activision Blizzard, SA will continue to find ways to keep listening to its community.
